result.summary: DIMENSION: fleet-desired admission chain + required-CI contract epoch. WHAT THE ADMIT JOB WRITES: `.github/workflows/fleet-desired.yml` job `admit` (emitted by `gunbc.fleet_desired_admission_workflow` `fleet_desired_admission_job`) runs `gunbc run --entry dag/gunbc/fleet/fleet_desired_admission.dag --function admit_fleet_desired_from_push_wet`, which writes a local script `target/fleet-desired-authorized-action.sh` rendered by `gunbc.fleet_desired_admission` `fleet_desired_authorized_action_script`; the next step executes it. On the advancing arm that script is `git push --force-with-lease=refs/fleet/desired:<observed prior> origin <accepted>:refs/fleet/desired`. So `contents: write` is spent on ONE thing: advancing the git ref `refs/fleet/desired` on origin (gunb-ai/gunbc). Not a committed file, not a tag, not a GCS object. Creation is refused by construction (`gunbc.fleet_main_revision` `decide_fleet_desired_advance` -> `InitialFleetDesiredCreationNotAuthorized`), so the job only ever moves an existing ref forward. WHO READS `refs/fleet/desired`: the only ls-remote reader is `gunbc.fleet_desired_observe` `observe_admitted_revision`. Its callers: (1) `gunbc.fleet_desired_admission` itself (CAS prior); (2) `gunbc.fleet_converge_cli` `converge_cli_output` self route via `fleet_revision_standing` -- DEAD ROUTE: its own `gunbc_converge_cli_stage0_receiver_disposition` Terminal row says no receiver exists, and `gunbc.cli_dispatch_surface` binds the `converge` verb to `gunbc.fleet_converge_plan_cli` `fleet_converge_operator_cli_entry`, not to this module; only `fleet_converge_cli_witness_test` calls it; (3) `gunbc.live_deploy.deployed_tree_report` `deployed_tree_report_for_context` -- observe-only, invoked by no workflow or instrument (plan row `deploy_convergence_observed_side` states no execution of `deployed_tree_report_ci_wet` has occurred); (4) `gunbc.roadmap_launch_deployment_cli` `read_desired_hex` -- invoked ONLY by fleet-converge.yml mode `rlm_launch_deployment_receipt` (`gunbc.fleet_converge_workflow` `fleet_converge_rlm_launch_deployment_receipt_job`), i.e. inside the automation being deleted. fleet-converge.yml itself never reads the ref (grep for fleet/desired, ls-remote, fleet_desired in that file: empty) and none of the `--function` entries it runs imports `fleet_desired_observe`. `gunbc converge` does NOT read it. THE DASHBOARD does not read it at runtime: `gunbc.roadmap_dashboard_instance` carries `fleet_desired_ref_name` into `fleet_admitted_revision_source` -> `HostDashboardInstance.admitted_revision`, and that field is read by no production code (only `roadmap_dashboard_instance_witness_test`); `gunbc.roadmap_launch_admission` `launch_gate_revision` consumes `LocalTreeRevision` (git rev-parse HEAD), not the ref; `gunbc.roadmap_belt_actuate` imports `FleetRevisionStanding` but never uses it and its annotation records that `fleet_revision_standing` stopped being consulted on 2026-09-05. CONSEQUENCE: after the admit job is deleted there is no live production reader of the ref outside the fleet automation. EPOCH: `gunbc.required_ci_contract_epoch` has exactly four non-test consumers: `gunbc.fleet_revision_acceptance` (requires the value), `gunbc.required_ci_epoch_observation` (looks up the env key), `gunbc.compiler_gate_workflow` `compiler_gate_workflow` env (the LIVE emitter of witnesses.yml, line 22 `GUNBC_REQUIRED_CI_CONTRACT_EPOCH: 2026-10-09.1`) and `gunbc.witness_floor_workflow` `witness_floor_workflow` env (NOT live: `gunbc.generated_artifact_emit` maps `WitnessFloorYamlArtifact` to `expected_compiler_gate_yml`; `expected_witness_floor_yml` is consumed only by three tests). If the admission chain is deleted, nothing reads the value or the key: no step, script or Rust reads `$GUNBC_REQUIRED_CI_CONTRACT_EPOCH` (grep empty), so the epoch becomes a datum written into witnesses.yml and parsed by nobody -- a §3c dangling declaration -- plus prose citations in the `compiler_gate_workflow` header, `gunbc.design_document` (DESIGN.md Building & checks) and `gunbc.rung_drop` `v1_required_lanes_withdrawn`. `gunbc.fleet_desired_observe` must be SPLIT, not deleted whole: its local-HEAD half (`LocalTreeRevision`, `local_tree_revision`) has four production consumers outside the automation (`gunbc.dispatch_preflight`, `gunbc.roadmap_belt_actuate`, `gunbc.roadmap_launch_admission`, `gunbc.roadmap_served_observation`). No host-Rust consumer exists for anything in this dimension. None of the chain's witness tests is in `v2.workflow.required_floor` `required_gate_prefixes`, and per the 2026-10-09 drop no job runs `claim_executor --required-ci`, so deleting the root breaks nothing on the required path: enumeration above is the census.

result.summary: Census of every job emitted into .github/workflows/fleet-converge.yml (11 jobs, authority gunbc.fleet_converge_workflow fleet_converge_jobs / fleet_converge_job_edges) and .github/workflows/fleet-desired.yml (1 job, authority gunbc.fleet_desired_admission_workflow fleet_desired_admission_job), read in full from the YAML plus the emitting authorities where the YAML is opaque. Shape: a `build` job produces a verified 16-binary release pack (or the compiler pair for four modes) and every other job except `mtcollins1-boot` consumes it via `needs: [build]`; the shared `fleet-converge` job carries ~70 workflow_dispatch modes, each one `gunbc run --entry <dag> --function <fn>` on the runner pinned to the `host` input (srv1..srv4), federated as fleet-cloud-convergence@gunbai-secrets through WIF pool github-fleet-convergence and with the fleet SSH key (Secret Manager fleet-automation-ssh-key/versions/1) in an in-run ssh-agent; eight dedicated jobs exist because they need their own OIDC pool/environment (mtcollins1-boot, gcp-iam-converge, namecheap-observe, printer), their own runner (host-reset-return), or a receipt chain keyed on earlier Actions run ids (dashboard-deploy, approval-broker-dark-install, microvm-controller-install, rlm-launch-deployment-receipt). The by-hand inheritance is simpler than the YAML suggests: for plan/apply/dashboard-deploy an operator-local route ALREADY EXISTS and is the modeled one -- `gunbc converge --host <host> --mode plan|apply|deploy` (gunbc.cli_dispatch_surface gunbc_fleet_converge_operation_binding -> gunbc.fleet_converge_plan_cli fleet_converge_operator_cli_entry -> fleet_converge_local_plan_wet / fleet_converge_local_apply_wet / gunbc.live_deploy.apply live_deploy_apply_srv1_operator_local_wet) -- and every other mode is the same `gunbc run --entry ... --function ...` argv executed on the named host with the named Secret Manager version materialized by the operator's own principal instead of WIF. Three things cannot be done by hand as modeled: the WIF providers admit only this workflow's OIDC claims (gunbc.auth.oidc_claim_pins fleet_converge_workflow_claim_pins pins workflow_ref to fleet-converge.yml@main and event_name=workflow_dispatch), the three srv1 install/transaction entries are hard-bound to the CI runner principal (gunbc.ci_deploy_access ci_deploy_srv1_access) and the transaction one refuses outside Actions by construction, and `gunbc converge` refuses every `--target`, so the 20 spark_* modes have no operator-local verb and fall back to raw `gunbc run` argv. fleet-desired.yml is a separate authority (push-to-main admission that CAS-pushes refs/fleet/desired, read by gunbc.fleet_desired_observe, gunbc.dispatch_preflight, gunbc.roadmap_dashboard_instance and gunbc.roadmap_launch_deployment_cli) and whether it is inside the operator's ruling is an open question.
